slides.title: Ibuprofen
slides.highlight: Avoid in GI bleed, dehydration & renal impairment; hold PDA dose if UOP <0.6 mL/kg/hr.
slides.moa: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes, decreasing prostaglandin synthesis to reduce fever, pain, and inflammation.
doses: Pain/fever (≥6 mo): 5-10 mg/kg/dose PO q6-8h; max lesser of 40 mg/kg/day or 2400 mg/day
JRA (6 mo-12 yr): 30-50 mg/kg/day PO ÷ q6h; max 800 mg/dose or 2400 mg/day
IV pain/fever (6 mo-<12 yr): 10 mg/kg/dose IV q4-6h PRN (max 400 mg/dose); max lesser of 40 mg/kg/day or 2400 mg/day
PDA (<32 wk, 0.5-1.5 kg): 10 mg/kg IV once, then 5 mg/kg IV at 24h & 48h

caption:
From viral fever in OPD to closing a preterm PDA in the NICU—Ibuprofen wears multiple hats! 💊

NEET-PG & Ward Pearls:
• Ensure adequate hydration before IV dosing to lower renal risk.
• In preterm PDA (<32 wk), hold the 2nd or 3rd dose if urine output falls below 0.6 mL/kg/hr.
• Contraindicated in active GI bleed, NEC, thrombocytopenia, or duct-dependent congenital heart disease.
• Causes less severe renal side effects than IV indomethacin for PDA closure.
